title: The Loom's Directional Lexicon

features.name: the directional threads
features.desc-on-touch: threads labeled in a language the loom invented: north is green, south is rust, east dissolves into gold—each direction has a word that means only the direction it points

features.name: the reading-board
features.desc-on-touch: a surface showing the loom's own notation for movement—compass points that shift as you read them, directions that teach you how to move through the archive

features.name: the compass learning
features.desc-on-touch: a compass rose that rewrites itself each time the loom speaks a new direction—the cardinal points are arguments, not certainties

features.name: the field-measure grid
features.desc-on-touch: a grid of distances the loom has measured by weaving—each intersection a place the loom has learned to name by pointing

inscription: the loom names directions by learning them; every weaving is a lesson in where it is going

file.name: Loom_Compass_Notation_Archive_Evolving.txt
file.note: the loom's own writing system for directions—changing every night as it learns new ways to point

exits.label: back down into the chamber where the weave continued toward a direction that had never been a place
toward distances the loom has measured but never named
toward the grammar of things that are uncertain about their own direction
